subject.title: [Bug]: Performance degradation in session memory sync: full delete-reinsert pattern for growing JSONL files

question: Should OpenClaw implement true incremental session-memory chunk preservation now, and if so should maintainers sponsor a fresh implementation or try to salvage https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/75179?
rationale: The bug is source-reproducible, but the durable design touches session-state correctness, chunk overlap identity, batching, and SQLite index semantics, and the existing candidate PR is conflicting and unproven.

options.title: Sponsor fresh incremental design
options.body: Keep this issue canonical and ask for a new implementation against current memory_index_* tables and source-wide batching, with upgrade and long-session proof.

options.title: Adopt and repair the open PR
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/75179 as source material only if maintainers are willing to resolve conflicts, update it to current schema, and require real behavior proof.

options.title: Accept batching as enough for now
options.body: Explicitly decide that source-wide batching and dirty-threshold behavior are the supported optimization for this release cycle, then close or re-scope the incremental request.

recommendation.title: Sponsor fresh incremental design
recommendation.body: Keep this issue canonical and ask for a new implementation against current memory_index_* tables and source-wide batching, with upgrade and long-session proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent memory/session identity and transcript-corpus work makes this the strongest routing candidate for deciding the current schema and batching-compatible design.
